newsitem.title: INDIA: TENNIS-WASHINGTON STRETCHED BY LITTLE-KNOWN BULGARIAN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WASHINGTON STRETCHED BY LITTLE-KNOWN BULGARIAN.

text.p: Third-seeded American MaliVai Washington was forced to work hard for his 7-5 6-7 6-3 victory over little known Bulgarian Orlin Stanoychev in the first round of the Indian Open on Tuesday.
Washington, 1996 Wimbledon losing finalist now ranked 26th in the world, struggled with the heat and humidity in the southern Indian city before prevailing against the 114th-ranked Bulgarian.
The heat took its toll on Sweden's Lars Jonsson, who retired exhausted during the third set of his encounter with Marco Mengeschincheri of Italy.
The 209th-ranked Mengeschincheri, who had won the opening set 6-0 but lost the second 4-6, was leading 4-1 when the 150th-ranked Larsson told the referee that he could not continue.

Top seed and Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands sailed into the second round with a 6-4 6-4 victory over Swede Thomas Nydahl while Pat Cash of Australia swept aside India's Mahesh Bhupathi 6-1 6-3.
India'a Olympic bronze medallist Leander Paes disappointed local fans as he suffered an ignominious 6-1 6-2 first round defeat by Argentine Gaston Etlis.
